sizes.title: Agents alive, world by world
sizes.caption: Each line is one world, its agents after each game (means over 50 iterations). Orange: the ten worlds of Experiment 19, whose mates are drawn only among neighbours with a living child; grey: Experiment 17's ten, any neighbour a mate, to 10,000 iterations, and the five of them Experiment 18 played on.
sizes.recipe:
**Runs.** The ten runs of Experiment 19 — B2 at 10,000 tokens with brains mixed at birth and the mate drawn only among neighbours with a living child (`mix_mates` = `parents`), seeds 1 to 10, 20,000 iterations (`python3 gol_lab.py run E19`) — beside Experiment 17's ten runs with any neighbour as mate, to 10,000 iterations, and the five of them Experiment 18 played on, read to 20,000.

**Data.** From each run's `stats.jsonl`.

1. Read the agents after each game (`nodes`, phase 2).
2. Average over stretches of 50 iterations.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py mixparents`.

poor.title: Agents holding three tokens or fewer
poor.caption: Each band is the worlds of one experiment — the median, the middle half and nine in ten — every 500 iterations: the share of their agents holding one, two or three tokens. Grey: Experiment 17's ten worlds to 10,000, and the five Experiment 18 played on; a world that died out leaves the band when it does.
poor.recipe:
**Runs.** The ten runs of Experiment 19 — B2 at 10,000 tokens with brains mixed at birth and the mate drawn only among neighbours with a living child (`mix_mates` = `parents`), seeds 1 to 10, 20,000 iterations (`python3 gol_lab.py run E19`) — beside Experiment 17's ten runs with any neighbour as mate, to 10,000 iterations, and the five of them Experiment 18 played on, read to 20,000.

**Data.** From each run's whole worlds kept every 500 iterations (`archive/world_<iteration>.npz`).

1. Read every agent's tokens in each whole world.
2. Count those holding three or fewer, as a share of all.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py mixparents`.

verdict.title: Experiment 19 at iteration 20,000
verdict.caption: Each dot is a world at iteration 20,000, read from the whole world kept then. Left: the share of its agents holding three tokens or fewer; the thesis asked that the median of the ten be below 0.66, the least of B2's ten worlds at 10,000 iterations. Right: how many of the seven marks of Chapter 46's health bar each world meets.
verdict.recipe:
**Runs.** The ten runs of Experiment 19 — B2 at 10,000 tokens with brains mixed at birth and the mate drawn only among neighbours with a living child (`mix_mates` = `parents`), seeds 1 to 10, 20,000 iterations (`python3 gol_lab.py run E19`) — beside Experiment 17's ten runs with any neighbour as mate, to 10,000 iterations, and the five of them Experiment 18 played on, read to 20,000.

**Data.** From each run's whole world kept at 20,000 (`archive/world_020000.npz`) and `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/e19_health.json` (`research/oee/checks/e17_health.py --family B2-10000-bcc1bc`).

1. Count the agents holding three tokens or fewer, as a share of all.
2. Measure the seven marks as `research/atlas/profile.py` does.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py mixparents`.

breeding.title: Who could have a child, and who has one
breeding.caption: Left: the share of the agents that could have a child — 11 tokens or more and fewer than 8 links. Right: the births of the next 50 iterations, per iteration, per hundred such agents, on a logarithmic axis. Each band is an experiment's worlds every 500 iterations — the median, the middle half and nine in ten.
breeding.recipe:
**Runs.** The ten runs of Experiment 19 — B2 at 10,000 tokens with brains mixed at birth and the mate drawn only among neighbours with a living child (`mix_mates` = `parents`), seeds 1 to 10, 20,000 iterations (`python3 gol_lab.py run E19`) — beside Experiment 17's ten runs with any neighbour as mate, to 10,000 iterations, and the five of them Experiment 18 played on, read to 20,000.

**Data.** From each world kept whole every 500 iterations, and each run's births (`research/oee/checks/e17_breeding.py`, `GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/e17_breeding.json` and `e19_breeding.json`).

1. In each whole world, count the agents with 11 tokens or more and fewer than 8 links.
2. Read the births of the 50 reproduction phases that follow.
3. Divide their mean per iteration by the agents counted.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py mixparents`.

evolution.title: Do later brains beat earlier ones?
evolution.caption: Each dot is a world: the share of a world the later era's brains hold after 100 iterations against the earlier era's, the mean of two contests, one in each era's world; the bar is the median world. 1,000/500: the brains of iteration 1,000 against those of 500. Orange: Experiment 19; grey: Experiment 17, any neighbour a mate.
evolution.recipe:
**Runs.** The ten runs of Experiment 19 — B2 at 10,000 tokens with brains mixed at birth and the mate drawn only among neighbours with a living child (`mix_mates` = `parents`), seeds 1 to 10, 20,000 iterations (`python3 gol_lab.py run E19`) — beside Experiment 17's ten runs with any neighbour as mate, to 10,000 iterations, and the five of them Experiment 18 played on, read to 20,000.

**Data.** From each run's whole worlds (`GraphOfLifeRuns/.pilots/e19_T100.json` and `e17_T100.json`).

1. Seat the brains of the two eras on alternate agents of each era's world and play it on for 100 iterations (`research/oee/checks/rejudge.py`).
2. Count the agents the later era's brains hold at the end, as a share of all.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py mixparents`.
